flashcards.a: Chain of Responsibility, Command, Interpreter, Iterator, Mediator, Memento, Observer, State, Strategy, Template Method, Visitor.

flashcards.q: What is Strategy reduced to in Python and modern Java?
flashcards.a: A function/lambda parameter -- e.g. sorted(data, key=...). Build a class only if the strategy needs to carry non-trivial state/config alongside its behavior.

flashcards.q: What does the State pattern actually buy you, beyond the class hierarchy ceremony?
flashcards.a: An explicit, checkable valid-transition graph (a dict/map from current state to allowed next states) that makes illegal transitions (e.g. PENDING -> DELIVERED skipping payment) loud errors instead of silent bugs from scattered if-statements.

flashcards.q: Name the two classic production bugs in a naive Observer/event-bus implementation.
flashcards.a: 1) Mutating the live subscriber list while iterating it (a handler unsubscribes mid-notification) -- fix by iterating a copy. 2) One handler's uncaught exception aborting notification to all subsequent subscribers -- fix by catching/logging per-handler and continuing.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't Command collapse to a plain function the way Strategy does?
flashcards.a: A function can't be queued, serialized, logged, retried, or undone without extra machinery. Making the action itself an object with execute()/undo() gives you all of that for free -- the object-ness is the whole point (job queues, CLI subcommands, agent tool-call logs, undo stacks).

flashcards.q: When does Visitor still earn its keep over pattern matching (match/switch)?
flashcards.a: When the type set is FIXED and stable but the set of OPERATIONS grows over time (e.g. a compiler's AST visited by many passes) -- each new Visitor is a self-contained class touching zero existing node classes. Pattern matching wins the opposite case: operations fixed/few, types grow (adding a case per match site instead).

flashcards.q: Why were java.util.Observer/Observable deprecated in Java 9?
flashcards.a: Observable is a concrete class (forces single inheritance), not thread-safe, and uses raw Object for arguments (pre-generics design). Replaced by PropertyChangeListener or an application event bus (Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher, Guava's EventBus).

flashcards.q: What is Template Method really, in modern terms?
flashcards.a: Plain method overriding / framework hook methods -- barely a 'pattern' beyond naming the intent (fixed skeleton, overridable steps). Django class-based views, JUnit setUp/tearDown, torch.nn.Module.forward are all this, unnamed.

flashcards.q: Why is hand-writing __iter__/__next__ usually wrong in Python?
flashcards.a: A generator function (yield-based) does the identical job with automatic state tracking and no manual StopIteration handling. Write the class-based version only when building a reusable container type needing independent re-iteration or extra methods (reset/peek) a generator can't expose.

Strategy: the CALLER picks the algorithm per invocation, no persistent identity needed. State: the OBJECT ITSELF owns which behavior applies, and it changes as a side effect of events over the object's lifecycle.

flashcards.q: When is Mediator justified, and what's its main failure mode?
flashcards.a: When N objects would otherwise need N^2 direct references to coordinate (chat server relaying clients, saga orchestrator). Failure mode: the mediator itself absorbs all coordination logic and becomes a God Object if business rules creep in rather than staying pure routing/sequencing.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't naive Memento (full deep-copy per command) scale, and what's the production alternative?
flashcards.a: Deep-copying full object state on every command is expensive for large documents/graphs. Production undo systems store the inverse command (Command-based undo) or incremental diffs, falling back to full snapshots only at coarser checkpoints -- exactly what LangGraph/Temporal checkpointing does at the framework level.

flashcards.q: Map orchestration-vs-choreography (saga pattern) onto GoF behavioral pattern names.
flashcards.a: Orchestration = Mediator (a central coordinator routes/sequences calls). Choreography = Observer/pub-sub (each service reacts to events with no central coordinator).

flashcards.q: Why is Interpreter rarely hand-rolled in application code today?
flashcards.a: If you need a real grammar, a parser generator (ANTLR, Lark) or an embedded language is used instead of a hand-rolled class-per-grammar-rule hierarchy. Interpreter's structure survives unnamed in query builders (SQLAlchemy select() builds and walks an AST) and rule engines.
